text:
Recalino is a personal English learning workspace for adults aged 18 and over. It keeps each class’s materials together and turns them into notes and practice. The current MVP centres on the learner’s own class content.

text:
The initial audience is adult English learners who want relevant practice after class. Recalino addresses the friction of scattered materials and limited review time. These are product design hypotheses. The project has not yet established them through market research or measured learner outcomes.

text:
The MVP supports browser recording with pause and resume, local recovery, and uploads of audio, images, PDFs and text. Learners can review sources and quota use before processing. The preview simulates recording and does not activate the microphone. Real recording requires the permission of people present. Long recording tests on target devices remain incomplete.

text:
Recalino builds notes from a structured knowledge model and records the origin of each content section. Editing creates a new version, which the learner can compare with earlier versions. Regeneration offers proposed changes and preserves the learner’s edits until they choose to accept a replacement. The examples shown here use synthetic content.

text:
Recalino distinguishes class content from additional AI explanation and the learner’s own edits. Points attributed to the class need valid source references, such as an audio timestamp or document page. These references help the learner check a point against the source. They do not guarantee educational accuracy.

text:
The live review flow uses FSRS. Learners recall the answer before revealing it, then record their response so the scheduler can choose the next review time. The interface supports Simple and Advanced modes, undoing the latest response, and a time goal. The preview’s Forgot and Remembered controls demonstrate the interaction without changing a real account’s schedule.

text:
The MVP provides standalone HTML notes and APKG card exports. HTML notes can be read in a browser without connecting to Recalino. Synthetic APKG data has passed an Anki import test, including a repeat import without duplicates. The preview does not connect to the real APKG exporter. Anki synchronisation, importing from Anki, and fully offline review remain outside the MVP scope.

text:
Sources are private. The original recording stays on the learner’s device, and the server keeps a transcription copy for no more than 24 hours after successful transcription. Deletion controls distinguish removing a source from a class, deleting its file, and deleting linked content. Legal text and the data processing agreement still need approval before a pilot with real class content. The project has no independent security or compliance certification.

text:
As of 4 October 2026, the project reports the main MVP features as implemented and checked with automated tests and synthetic data. The next stage is a controlled learner pilot, human evaluation of educational quality, and completion of legal and data approvals. Synthetic examples do not establish learning outcomes or retention rates. Real class processing still depends on the relevant approvals.
